poster.description:
Across the mountains of Kailasa and the temples of the human world unfolds a vast tapestry of devotion, cosmic love, and divine fury: the sacred legends of Lord Shiva. In this retelling of the Siva Puranam, ancient myth and fervent bhakti meet in stories where gods, demons, sages, and humble devotees all move within the orbit of the great ascetic god.

The book journeys from the celestial marriage of Shiva and the devoted Sati to the tragedy of her self‑immolation at her father Daksha’s sacrificial rite—an insult that unleashes Shiva’s terrifying wrath upon the universe. It follows Sati’s rebirth as Parvati, whose fierce austerities win Shiva’s heart and restore the divine union upon which cosmic balance depends. From their union arises Skanda, the radiant warrior child destined to defeat the tyrant demon Taraka and restore order to heaven and earth.

Alongside these sweeping cosmic dramas are luminous tales of human devotion. Saints and outcasts alike seek the grace of Shiva: the longing of Nandanar to behold Nataraja in Chidambaram, the miraculous power of the child saint Jnana Sambandhar, and the shocking hospitality of Siriyala, whose willingness to sacrifice everything reveals the depth of true faith. Again and again, Shiva appears in disguise, testing hearts and overturning worldly hierarchy.

Filled with miracles, fierce asceticism, divine romance, and spiritual teaching, the Siva Puranam presents Shiva as both terrifying and compassionate—the destroyer who is also the source of liberation. These stories invite readers into a universe where devotion can move mountains, gods walk among mortals, and the path to the divine may begin anywhere, with anyone who calls upon the Lord of Kailasa.
poster.cover_scene: In ornate Indian miniature style, Lord Shiva and Parvati sit together upon Mount Kailasa surrounded by gods, sages, and devoted mortals while celestial rivers, temple spires, and swirling halos suggest the vast mythic world shaped by Shiva’s power and grace.
